service.name: Corporate retreat entertainment in Aspen
service.serviceType: Live music for corporate retreats and incentive events
service.description: Live music for corporate retreats and private celebrations at Aspen venues, solo through quartet, with travel and lodging.

faqs.q: What does live music cost in Aspen?
faqs.a: There are three lines, itemised. The first is the fee for the music, with sound support that's the right size for the venue inside it. The second is travel, because Aspen is roughly four hours from Denver each way over passes. The third is a night's lodging at cost, because a band that played a late set isn't driving that road home. A retreat budget goes through finance, and a quote that separates the three is easier to forward and approve.

faqs.q: Why is lodging on an Aspen quote?
faqs.a: Because an Aspen date is a two-day trip for the band. The drive runs about four hours in good conditions and longer in winter, and a band that finishes late isn't driving mountain highways home that night. Lodging bills at cost, on its own line.

faqs.q: How long is the drive from Denver, really?
faqs.a: About four hours when the roads cooperate. Independence Pass closes seasonally, so winter dates run the long way through Glenwood Springs, and weather can stretch any of it. We build that margin into the load-in day.

faqs.q: Can the party run outdoors in Aspen?
faqs.a: Yes, until eight in the evening. Outdoor amplified sound at a private event was reported capped at 80 dBA at the perimeter, between 9am and 8pm, when we checked, with neighbours within 250 feet owed seven days' notice. Evenings move indoors from there, and we confirm the current figures with your venue.

faqs.q: What size fits an Aspen dinner?
faqs.a: A duo or a trio holding 65 to 72 dBA at the nearest table is the working answer for dinner at a venue like The Little Nell or the Hotel Jerome. A quartet is the booking when a dance floor is the objective.
